key_insight: A non-planar 3×3 crossbar Josephson qubit realizes a flux-tunable Z_3 combinatorial gauge symmetry, enabling a new route toward gauge-theory and spin-liquid physics in circuit QED.
engineering_relevance: This design expands superconducting qubit architectures beyond planar layouts, creating a tunable platform for exploring higher-dimensional connectivity and lattice gauge simulation.
method: Built a non-planar 3×3 crossbar Josephson array inside a superconducting cavity
Tuned magnetic flux to reach and probe the Z_3 gauge-symmetry point
Compared measured spectra with neural-network-generated variational quantum states
evidence_signal: The excitation spectrum matches neural-network predictions closely, and cavity-driven symmetry breaking shows restoration of symmetry at the combinatorial gauge-symmetry point.
watch_item: Fine-structure splittings near the symmetry point suggest possible weak tunneling or fabrication-induced symmetry breaking, which may limit ideal Z_3 behavior.
paper_title: Nonplanar qubit with tunable gauge symmetry
